clue.text: It makes perfect sacrifice, deed being hidden

indicators.note: the deed is hidden within the sacrifice, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the price paid for something is what you sacrifice for it
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A sermon on noble sacrifice: the good deed done quietly, out of sight, is what makes a person perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes perfect' leans on the saying 'practice makes perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'practice makes perfect' supplies the definition: repeated rehearsal is the thing that perfects a skill.

clue.text: Feeble joke — start to yawn

parts.note: a pun is a joke based on wordplay

indicators.note: the start of the word yawn gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A groaner of a joke that only gets a yawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny describes something weak or small, a close synonym of feeble.

clue.text: French plane, one ditched in river

indicators.note: one is ditched, dropped out of the French word

parts.note: avion is French for aeroplane
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French aircraft crash-lands in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditched' plays on a plane ditching in water, but here it means something is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is a river in England, flowing through Stratford, one of several of that name.

clue.text: Old boy, taken in by baddy, gives expression of resignation

indicators.note: the old boy is taken inside the baddy's word

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible, nasty person
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil, conned by a villain, sighs and accepts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'too bad' is a shrug of acceptance, an idiom meaning nothing can be done about it.

clue.text: Weather expert with cold capital to record is taking temperature

indicators.note: is takes on the temperature, which is attached to it at the end

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru
taken as written
a log is a record, as kept on a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forecaster in a chilly capital city logs readings, noting the temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A climatologist studies climate, the long-term patterns of weather, so is a scientist expert in it.

clue.text: Painful bill — object, spending time

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: the object spends, or gives up, its time letter

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a hefty bill after spending so much time.
explanation.definitionFit: Aching describes a part of the body that hurts with a dull, persistent pain, so it is sore.

clue.text: Schedule a novice driver needs to finish up in vehicle

indicators.note: these pieces are placed in the vehicle's word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car
to finish up is to end

explanation.surface: A learner driver has to end the lesson sitting in the car on time.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a list of dates and events, a timetable or programme of appointments.

clue.text: Is artist chosen son from chosen people?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the elite are the chosen few

explanation.surface: Asks whether an artist's favoured son comes from the Biblical chosen people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites of the Bible are the people of Israel, described in scripture as chosen by God.

clue.text: Member of family can let urge get out of control

indicators.note: the letters run riot and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative who cannot keep his impulses in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-uncle is a parent's uncle, a relation two generations up in one's family tree.

clue.text: It's new in some lingo

indicators.note: new letters are made from the old ones by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A coinage: something freshly minted in a particular language.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a freshly coined word or expression entering a language, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: A mountain — it'll spread across more than one country

indicators.note: the letters are spread about into a different order

explanation.surface: A mountain range big enough to straddle borders between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Multinational describes something involving or operating in several nations, as a company might.

clue.text: Way river runs into Irish port

indicators.note: the river runs into the way, going inside it

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road

explanation.surface: A road and a river converging at an Irish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a harbour town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, with ferries to Scotland.

clue.text: Vehicle has all soldiers heading off with speed in upper region

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the soldiers lose their first letter

parts.note: men are soldiers, as opposed to officers
to belt is to go at speed

explanation.surface: A van carries all the troops away at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Van Allen belts are zones of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field, high up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Component in dinner I get possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Wondering what goes into the dinner one is served.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one part of a mixture or recipe, so a constituent element.

clue.text: Fiddling at wrist, chap may let one slip off

definitions.text: Fiddling at wrist, chap may let one slip off

indicators.note: fiddling with the letters rearranges them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the letter that slips off from the pool

explanation.surface: A man fiddling with something on his wrist risks letting it fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AT WRIST CHAP but let I (one) slip off the pool of letters: the remaining ten form the answer, which is also what the fidgeting chap might lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is held to the wrist by a band, which a fidgeting wearer could unfasten so the watch falls.

clue.text: Well turned-out exhibits at cattle show?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tidy and smartly dressed
second meaning: an old word for cattle, the animals shown at a cattle show

explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle or oxen, still found in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tidy and smart, and is also an archaic plural noun for bovine animals.

clue.text: Control comes with financial gift — main way to get in

indicators.note: the main way gets inside the gift

parts.note: a donation is a gift of money
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Power that comes from a donation: buying a route into influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, read here as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is power or rule over others, so it is a form of control.

clue.text: Painless barking for dogs

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: Barking is harmless enough for dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like what the dogs do, but it is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniels are a breed group of gun dogs with long drooping ears.

clue.text: One of two is half expressing mutual relationship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in mathematics, one over two, the inverse of two, is a half
second meaning: given and received in return by each party

explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads as a fraction: the inverse of 2 is one half.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the mathematical inverse of a number and also describes feelings or actions returned in kind.

clue.text: What the devil did is cruel

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective survives mainly in the phrase 'at one fell swoop'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of falling, as Satan did, and an old adjective for savage.

clue.text: Looking angry, fellow being caught and put back inside

indicators.note: the fellow is caught within the angry word

parts.note: a red face shows anger
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An enraged man is arrested and sent back to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To remand is to send an accused back into custody while awaiting trial.

clue.text: I'd sneezed — it's bad — could antihistamines make one this?

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad state, jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A hay-fever sufferer complains of a nasty sneezing fit and wonders whether pills will help.
explanation.definitionFit: Antihistamines dull the body's allergic response, leaving the patient less sensitive to pollen and the like.

clue.text: President once with aspiration for boost

parts.note: an aspirate is the breathed sound H
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A former president with ambitions for a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A hike is a sharp increase, as in a price rise, so a boost.

clue.text: Cut width in layer

indicators.note: the width letter goes in the layer word

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming a width out of a layer of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, to chop or carve, as with an axe.

clue.text: Jane keeps one place for eggs

indicators.note: Jane's surname keeps one inside it

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jane keeps a single spot for her eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's or other bird of prey's nest, built high up, where it lays.

clue.text: Insecure in shelter, Argentinian lady turned over

parts.note: a tent is a shelter

indicators.note: the lady's name is turned over, read from the back

parts.note: Evita was Eva Peron, wife of the Argentine president

explanation.surface: A nervous camper finds an Argentinian woman upended in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means hesitant or uncertain, lacking confidence.

clue.text: Asian drunk, we hear — one in the pool?

indicators.note: says the answer sounds like the spoken phrase

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian, and pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk man from Asia, rumour has it, ended up in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests a swimming pool, but a typing pool was an office's bank of typists; 'pissed' is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices once kept a typing pool, a team of secretaries who typed documents for everyone.

clue.text: British lord, grand, a very long time in club

parts.note: lud is lord, as in 'm'lud' in court
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A British peer, wealthy, spends ages at his gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a London gentlemen's club, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy stick used as a weapon, a cudgel.
